subject: Information Theory
title: Conditional Entropy
description: A fast breakdown of Conditional Entropy for builders.

hook.text: How uncertain is tomorrow's weather given today's? Less uncertain. Conditional entropy measures how much less.

buildup.text: Conditional entropy H(Y|X) measures remaining uncertainty about Y after learning X.

discovery.text: If X and Y are independent, H(Y|X) = H(Y). Knowing one says nothing about the other.

twist.text: If X completely determines Y, H(Y|X) = 0. Zero remaining uncertainty—X tells you everything.

climax.text: Mutual information is the gap: I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X). What X told you about Y.

punchline.text: Condition on what you know. Measure what's left.

quiz.question: When does H(Y|X) equal zero?
options: When X and Y are independent
When knowing X completely determines Y
